ingredients.name: Canned mackerel or tuna
ingredients.notes: 1 large can; drained thoroughly, large bones and dark skin removed

ingredients.name: Starchy potatoes
ingredients.notes: boiled in salted water until just fork-tender, drained, cooled before mashing

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: finely chopped; the finer the chop, the less likely cutlets are to crack

ingredients.name: Green chillies
ingredients.notes: finely chopped; deseed for milder cutlets

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: freshly ground; a generous amount is important to the flavour

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: to taste; canned fish already carries salt

ingredients.name: Plain flour
ingredients.notes: for a thin pre-coat before the egg wash

ingredients.name: Fine dry breadcrumbs
ingredients.notes: fine breadcrumbs preferred over coarse for an even, crack-resistant crust

ingredients.name: Oil for deep frying
ingredients.notes: heat to 165-170C (330-340F); this lower temperature reduces cracking

steps.instruction: Boil the potatoes in salted water until just fork-tender, about 15-18 minutes. Drain and leave in the warm pot briefly to dry off excess moisture. Peel and mash until smooth. Set aside to cool completely.
Drain the canned fish thoroughly, pressing out all liquid. Remove large bones and dark skin. Break into flakes.

Heat a little oil in a pan. Saute the onion until soft, 3-4 minutes. Add garlic and ginger, cook 1 minute. Add the flaked fish, chilli powder, turmeric, black pepper, and green chillies. Stir and cook 2 minutes.
Add the cooled mashed potato and curry leaves. Mix until cohesive. Add lime juice and salt. Cook 1-2 minutes until dry and holds together -- a wet filling causes cutlets to crack.
Remove from heat and cool completely before shaping -- shaping warm filling significantly increases cracking risk.
Set up a breading station: flour, beaten egg, breadcrumbs. Roll the cooled filling into balls of about 30-40g each.
Coat each ball in flour, dip in egg, roll in breadcrumbs pressing firmly. For a crack-resistant crust, double-coat: dip in egg again and roll in breadcrumbs a second time.
Refrigerate the coated cutlets for 10-15 minutes before frying -- this firms up the coating and reduces cracking.
Heat oil to 165-170C (330-340F). Fry in small batches for 3-4 minutes, turning gently, until deep golden all over. Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with ketchup, chilli sauce, or lime.

source_site: loveandotherspices.com, cross-checked against theflavorbender.com, hungrylankan.com, islandsmile.org, kannammacooks.com, berrychik.com, and mylankanfoodjournal.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 7+ independent sources; highest-confidence entry for a deep-fried snack, with very strong agreement on anti-cracking technique
notes: Sri Lankan fish cutlets (maalu cutlets) are essentially croquettes -- a 'short eat' served at parties, high tea, and roadside cafes. Cracking during frying is the single most discussed failure mode across all sources; the agreed solutions are: cool the filling completely before shaping, keep the filling dry, use fine breadcrumbs, double-coat, and fry at 165-170C rather than 180-190C. Cutlets freeze extremely well unfried (single layer first, then container); fry straight from frozen when needed. Mackerel gives a stronger, more traditional flavour; tuna gives a milder result.
